evidence.field: 菜 entry; graphic analysis
evidence.text: The Han dictionary defines 菜 as edible vegetation and parses it as 艸 with 采 supplying the sound. This is an early explicit account of the graph’s structure, not independent proof of every historical detail.
evidence.title: 說文解字/01

evidence.field: 形義通解; graphic history and early spellings
evidence.text: The database analyzes 菜 as 艸 plus phonetic 采, with vegetable as its basic meaning. It reports bronze inscriptions using the graph for a place name and Qin slips writing the vegetable word as 采 in 采羹. It cites the Guoyu phrase 庶人食菜，祀以魚 and notes a later use for prepared food. The Qin spelling is evidence for an earlier spelling practice, not by itself evidence that the graph 菜 originated from 采.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 菜

evidence.source: Chen Jian, Fudan University Center for the Study of Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: Qin and Han slip attestations; disputed graph readings
evidence.text: The paper reports Qin Shuihudi legal slips’ 采羹 as 菜羹, plus Han silk and Zhangjiashan slip spellings of 菜 as 采. It also surveys disputed readings of some Spring and Autumn bronze and Warring States Chu graphs containing a 采-like element; those examples cannot simply be counted as early attestations of 菜. The author argues the older 采 spelling was common before 菜 became standard, while acknowledging the paleographic readings under discussion.
evidence.title: 陳劍：釋上博竹書和春秋金文的“羹”字異體

evidence.field: dating/context for Shuihudi Qin legal slips
evidence.text: The museum identifies the Shuihudi Qin Law Eighteen Types slips as Qin-period material, excavated from tomb 11 at Shuihudi in 1975. This dates the artifact context; the individual 菜/采 reading is supplied by paleographic scholarship rather than this collection record.
evidence.title: 睡虎地秦簡《秦律十八種》

evidence.field: 采 entry; component’s graphic analysis and semantics
evidence.text: For 采, the database describes oracle-bone forms with 爪 (hand) and either 木 or 果, interpreted as a hand picking fruit from a tree. It calls 采 the earlier graph for 採, with picking as the basic sense, and cites Shuowen’s 捋取也 and 从木从爪. This supports the source graph’s form and lexical sense; it does not prove that 菜’s word arose by derivation from the verb.
evidence.title: 漢語甲骨部件分析 — 爪

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction; semantic derivation proposal
evidence.text: Reports Zhengzhang’s 2003 Old Chinese reconstructions *sʰɯːs for 菜 and *sʰɯːʔ for 采, and separately lists Baxter–Sagart’s *s.r̥ˤəʔ-s for 菜. It proposes a derivation ‘what is gathered or plucked’ from 采 plus nominalizing *-s, citing Sagart (1999) and Schuessler (2007). This is a proposed word-history account, not established solely by the phonetic-component analysis; the different reconstructions belong to different systems.
evidence.title: 菜 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: phonetic comparison and Middle Chinese readings
evidence.text: Gives 采 as Mandarin cǎi and standard Cantonese coi2, with Middle Chinese tshojX and fanqie 倉宰切. It lists Zhengzhang’s *sʰɯːʔ and Baxter–Sagart’s *s.r̥ˤəʔ for 采. Within Zhengzhang’s system, the shared onset and rhyme with 菜, alongside 菜’s departing-tone reconstruction *-s, are compatible with a phonetic relationship; reconstructions are model-based comparisons, not direct pronunciations.
evidence.title: 采 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: modern and historical readings
evidence.text: Lists Standard Mandarin cài and Standard Cantonese coi3, and records Japanese on readings さい (sai) and kun reading な (na), and Korean 채 (chae). These are language-specific readings of the graph; the Japanese kun reading does not by itself establish a Japanese origin for the character or prove the chronology of Japanese meanings.
evidence.title: 菜 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Kotobank, drawing on 精選版日本国語大辞典 and 字通
evidence.field: dated Japanese senses and semantic development
evidence.text: The dictionary cites 菜 for edible herbs/greens in the eighth-century Man’yōshū, and gives a first cited example for the side-dish sense from 今昔物語集, dated approximately 1120. It says the native Japanese reading na was used broadly for side dishes in early Japanese, later replaced in general use by the Sino-Japanese reading sai; vegetables and side dishes are distinct senses. These dates concern Japanese usage, not the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 菜(サイ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.field: Chinese modern readings and historical phonology
evidence.text: Lists Standard Mandarin cài and Standard Cantonese coi3, and Middle Chinese Baxter transcription tshojH, corresponding to departing tone and Guangyun 倉代切. Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese form is *sʰɯːs; Baxter–Sagart’s is *s.r̥ˤəʔ-s. The difference reflects distinct reconstruction systems and should not be collapsed into one form.
evidence.title: 菜 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: phonological resource scope
evidence.text: The opened resource exposes separate fields for Guangyun/Qieyun, Baxter–Sagart 2011, and Schuessler’s ABC dictionary, but did not return a character-specific 菜 result in the inspected page. It therefore cannot be cited here as direct confirmation of a particular reconstruction.

evidence.field: Japanese readings and word/graph distinction

evidence.text: The scanned 菜 entry reads: “形声字。从艸，采声。本义是指蔬菜。” It quotes Shuowen, “菜，艸之可食者”; cites 《尔雅·广物》“菜谓之蔬” and 《论语·乡党》“虽疏食菜羹，瓜祭，必齐如也”; and says the character also refers to dishes collectively, with 荤菜、川菜 and a 《北史·胡叟传》 example. evidence.text: The entry analyzes 菜 as 艸 plus phonetic 采, with vegetables as its basic meaning. It reports bronze forms used as a place name, Qin slips writing the vegetable word as 采 in 采(菜)羹, and cites the Guoyu sentence “庶人食菜，祀以魚.” It also cites a 《北史·胡叟傳》 example for use as a collective term for dishes. It gives the picking sense and discusses the relationship of 采 and 採. This bears on 采’s own history; it does not by itself establish a derivation of the word 菜 from the verb ‘gather, pluck.’

It separately gives Baxter–Sagart 2014 forms 菜 /*s.r̥ˤəʔ-s/ and 采 /*s.r̥ˤəʔ/. These are system-specific reconstructions, not direct recordings; the page’s proposed derivation of 菜 as ‘what is gathered or plucked’ with a nominal suffix is not independently established by the phonetic analysis.

gaps: The exact earliest secure attestation of the full 菜 graph remains unclear: the inspected CUHK database reports bronze forms, including place-name use, but gives no inscription date or specimen details in the opened entry.
No securely identified oracle-bone form of 菜 was found in inspected material. Oracle-bone evidence for 采 does not establish an oracle-bone date for 菜.

Some Spring and Autumn bronze and Warring States Chu forms containing a 采-like element have contested readings. The Fudan paper explicitly notes prior mistaken readings and treats these separately from straightforward vegetable-word spellings.

The proposed lexical derivation of 菜 from 采 ‘gather/pluck’ plus nominalizing *-s is reported as a scholarly analysis, but this research did not inspect the cited Sagart 1999 and Schuessler 2007 argument in full. It remains separate from the graphic reading of 采 as 菜 in Qin slips.
The consulted source transcribes the Qin spelling as 采(菜), but a direct visual inspection of the relevant slip image and independent edition collation were not completed.

Chinese semantic chronology is only partly dated here: the Qin slip example supports a vegetable/food sense, and the CUHK source cites a Guoyu passage and a later Northern Wei food/dish usage. A comprehensive dated history of each Chinese sense was not established.

No evidence was found that the Japanese kun reading な marks a Japanese-created graph or establishes the date of the Japanese lexeme. Japanese sources do provide eighth-century and medieval cited examples, but dating of the lexeme itself remains open.
The EDOC character-specific lookup was not obtained from the opened interface. Reconstruction comparisons here rely on the opened dictionary entry and the primary Baxter–Sagart table.

Only one directly supported, reusable candidate was established: a modern vector redraw of a seal-script form. No ancient artifact photograph or verified bronze/Qin-slip glyph image with individual provenance and reuse information was established in this search.
